question: Does causal neighboring-marker geometry history improve held-out future deformation prediction beyond present velocity, full gradient and current geometry?
equations: 3D unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes, periodic box [-3,3)^3; unchanged parent numerics.Flow projection, rotational nonlinearity, viscosity and Heun integrator
initial_conditions: Independent random coefficients and phases on a fixed set of low Fourier modes, projected divergence-free, RMS speed normalized to 1. Same modes as parent perturb(), plus axis modes. These are NEW smooth initial conditions, not reruns of the original unresolved strain/tube start.
target: log(sigma_max(M(t+gap+horizon) inv(M(t+gap))))/horizon, delayed forward FTLE of the numerical interpolated velocity; no target integration interval at or before prediction time
event_threshold: Training-target quantile only; never re-quantile validation/test
models: Train-standardized ridge and logistic regression; validation selects regularization. Secondary matched HistGradientBoosting models use same depth, leaves, iterations and tuning grid in A and B.
controls: shuffled target labels in training only
interpretation: Exploratory pilot. No model or hypothesis selection on test scores. Resolution and viscosity variants are dependent sensitivity checks, not additional independent test runs. No causal/leadership/regularity claim. History can improve an incomplete observation, not add fundamental information to a complete deterministic state.
